c989db0d32fd.text: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification. The word of the year in the AI industry over 2026 has been “slop” — meaning low-quality output from a large language model. And with so much code being AI-generated now, avoiding slop has become a daily concern for software engineers. So how to do that? One way is to use formal verification systems , which use mathematical proofs and logic to verify the correctness of software or hardware. With AI’s growing prowess at solving math problems , there’s now a number of AI companies offering formal verification systems. debates.title: Riemann Hypothesis: AI-assisted vs human-only proofs
debates.summary: Two independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis appeared within hours — one by Anthropic's Levent Alpöge using Claude and formalized in Lean, another by Alessandro Masullo developed entirely by humans. The episode has shifted expert timelines dramatically and raised questions about AI's role in fundamental mathematics.

positions.stance: Notes that top forecasters have dramatically shortened their timelines — Metaculus now predicts May 2035, superforecasters see a 10% chance of another Millennium problem solved in 2026, while Terence Tao still estimates 2050 for human-AI collaboration.

debates.title: Agentic commerce: Walmart embraces while Amazon blocks
debates.summary: Walmart is actively embracing AI shopping agents while Amazon appears to be blocking them — a reversal of their e-commerce positions. New Stripe data suggests agentic shopping may be gaining real traction with surprisingly sticky usage.

positions.stance: Argues Walmart is determined not to repeat its e-commerce mistake by embracing agentic commerce early, while Amazon blocks agents; cites Stripe data showing agentic shopping is kicking off and surprisingly sticky.

debates.title: AI gains in unverifiable domains vs slop concerns
debates.summary: While models show large improvements in unverifiable domains like writing, business problems, design, and freelance tasks, the industry wrestles with a flood of low-quality 'slop' output — prompting interest in formal verification as a quality filter.

positions.stance: Presents human evaluation data showing very large AI gains in writing, business problems, design, and freelance tasks — domains without automatic verification — arguing progress extends beyond math and coding.
Flags a framework from binarybits.bsky.social as useful for thinking about AI capabilities in fields beyond verifiable domains like math and coding.

Reports that 'slop' has become the word of the year in AI, and formal verification systems from companies like Harmonic, Theorem, Axiom Math, and &Truth are emerging as a weapon against low-quality AI-generated code.

debates.title: Open weights slowdown linked to distillation restrictions
debates.summary: The rapid progress of open-weights models may be stalling because OpenAI and Anthropic have effectively ended easy distillation from their frontier models, removing a key acceleration mechanism for open competitors.

positions.stance: Suggests the effective end of easy distillation from OpenAI and Anthropic models may explain the relative slowdown in open-weights model progress, though the extent of distillation's role remains uncertain.
